card.statement:
The $p$ -curvature of the $D$ -module $M_{eq,reg}$ ( $M_{Kah,reg}$, resp.) are the endomorphisms of $D$ -modules given by the action of $s(R_{eq})\subseteq R_{eq,reg}$ ( $s(R_{Kah})\subseteq R_{Kah,reg}$, resp.) for the Artin–Schreier map $s:R^{(1)}\to R$ constructed in 4.4.

The fact that the action of $s(R)$ is an endomorphism of $D$ -modules (that is, covariant constancy of the $p$ -curvature) is an immediate consequence of the centrality of the image of $s$.

In the context of 3.21, the isomorphism of $D$ -modules $M_{eq,reg}\cong M^{!}_{Kah,reg}$ for symplectically dual pairs $X/k$ and $X^{!}/\mathbb{C}$ compatible with $R_{eq}\cong R^{!}_{Kah}$ implies the identification of $p$ -curvature operators for both $D$ -modules. Hence, in the case where $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ and $H^{*}_{T^{!}\times\mathbb{G}_{m}}(X^{!})$ are generated by (conical and cohomological, resp.) degree $2$ elements, 3.21 can be reduced to the following claims.
card.label: Definition 4.5

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
